messages.subject: [R-wiki] Scrambled pages
messages.body_plain:
Hello Gregor,

Yes, indeed, several pages were not correctly displayed. This is due a 
change in the caching mechanisms in the Wiki engine (I have recently 
upgraded it). Now, there is a double-caching mechanism which is much 
more efficient. However, it appears that the new mechanisms is sometimes 
fooled by caches written by the old engine. The solution is to refresh 
the faulty page in the cache. This is very easy to do. Just add 
"&purge=true" at the end of the URL and reload the page. The problem 
should be fixed permanently then.
Best,

Philippe Grosjean

messages.body_plain: Hello, Indeed, this would be very nice if someone could write a "SWeave2wiki" driver, perhaps inspired from the R2HTML "Sweave2HTML" driver. Eric Lecoutre (author of R2HTML) told me how easy it was to write such a driver, thanks to the good design of SWeave. I am currently working on the Rdconv adaptation to create wiki versions of R help pages. This is a priority for me, altogether with the refinement of the wiki pages presentation and navigation to get rid of the unpleasant "index" at left. And, as you have perhaps noticed, I can invest myself only a relatively limited time to such developments, currently. Thus, any help is warmly welcome. messages.body_plain:
Philippe Grosjean wrote:
> Hello,
> 
> Indeed, this would be very nice if someone could write a "SWeave2wiki"
> driver, perhaps inspired from the R2HTML "Sweave2HTML" driver. Eric
> Lecoutre (author of R2HTML) told me how easy it was to write such a
> driver, thanks to the good design of SWeave.
> 

> Philippe Grosjean

   It occurs to me there are actually two different tasks/programs here.
One is an Sweave driver for Wiki, which would allow one to maintain
wiki files with embedded R code that was executed, created figures,
etc..  The other (which is what Robin needs) converts from an existing
vignette (Sweave/Latex) to a wikified version; for this it's best (I
think) to work from the Sweave'd tex file and convert it to Wiki;
this is basically just regular expression conversion (which is what
all the existing latex2wiki scripts I've seen have been); it would
take a little bit of twiddling in Perl/Python/R ... ? but shouldn't
be too hard.  I will take a crack when I get a chance but no-one
should be holding their breath ...

   cheers
     Ben
